refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: This manual page describes additional vera features.

refsect2.title: system/network-online and system/networkmanager-wait-online
refsect2.para: The inittab command adds a requirement for the system/network-online target to every converted /etc/rc.d/rc.inet2 unit.
The installed system/networkmanager-wait-online unit can be enabled; it is then enabled as a dependency of system/network-online. This unit runs /usr/bin/nm-online when started.

If a system uses /etc/rc.d/rc.networkmanager then enabling system/networkmanager-wait-online delays system startup until NetworkManager initializes all network interfaces (all network interfaces have an active IP address). system/networkmanager-wait-online should not be enabled unless system/rc.M/rc.networkmanager is also enabled.

refsect2.title: Enabling cgroup v2 controllers and setting resources
refsect2.para: Slackware's default /etc/rc.d/rc.S script mounts all cgroup version 1 controllers in /sys/fs/cgroup.

Enabling the system/v2-controllers unit runs a script at system boot that enables cgroup v2 controllers after disabling the cgroup v1 controllers. This makes the controllers available to cgroup v2 containers. The cgroup v2 controllers are enabled for vera's units.
If version 1 controllers are turned off via a kernel boot parameter, the cgroup version 2 controllers are still enabled for vera's units.
With version 2 controllers enabled it is possible to set controller-managed resources using the set-resource command.

This limits system/rc.M/rc.sshd to 100 processes. The delete-resource command removes the unit's resource, reverting it to the Linux kernel's default.

The resources are actually set when a unit starts. The set-resource and delete-resource commands update the saved list of resources for each unit, and they take effect when the unit starts. If the unit is already running the new resources take effect the next time the unit starts.
See the Linux kernel's control group V2 documentation for a list of settable resources.

refsect3.title: Advanced resource control
refsect3.para: The set-resource command implements a generic interface to control group resources. vlad does not have any specific knowledge of any specific resource and what it does. set-resource performs a sanity check that only verifies that the specified resource interface file exists, and accepts any value. When a unit starts, each resource is set to its value, one by one.

Each resource is set by opening the interface file of the same name, as described in the Linux kernel's documentation, and writing the given value to it. Note that not every interface file described in the kernel's documentation is settable.

set-resource accepts multiple values. Multiple values are written to the interface file sequentially. Whether or not this has any effect is up to the controller; otherwise the last value becomes the effective one. If values are already set for a resource, set-resource replaces the values. There's also an add-resource command that sets additional values without removing any existing ones.
A newly-created container's resources are set in the order they were set via set-resource. The status command with the --resources option lists a unit's resources in the order they were set.

refsect3.title: Session resources
refsect3.para: Setting resources for a &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; unit applies those resources to every started session. The current implementation applies to all sessions uniformly. The same resources are set for every session, for every user, and every session type. There's currently no mechanism to set different resources for different users or session types.

refsect3.title: Summary of common resources
refsect3.para: This is a summary of the most common resources from the Linux kernel documentation. Consult the kernel's documentation for more information.

listitem.para: Setting cpu.idle to 1 schedules this unit at the lowest possible priority.
memory.max is the maximum amount of memory that can be used by the unit, in bytes.
Setting memory.oom.group to 1 results in all processes in the unit being killed by the OOM killer, instead of individual processes.
pids.max sets an upper limit on the number of processes that can be created in the unit.

refsect2.title: restart and reload commands for /etc/rc.d units
refsect2.para: The inittab command installs a unit for every script in /etc/rc.d that gets started from /etc/rc.d/rc.M and /etc/rc.d/rc.inet2. Each unit is named system/rc.M/name.

Each /etc/rc.d script is scanned and heuristically determined if it supports a restart and/or a reload operation. If so, then a restart and/or a reload command is included in the corresponding unit specification file.
For example: vlad restart system/rc.M/rc.sshd executes /etc/rc.d/rc.sshd restart in this unit's container.
